## Proposed change
<!--

  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

When Alexa issues a command to a Hue hub; it immediately queries the hub for the entity's state.to confirm if the command was successful.
It expects the state to be effective immediately.
There may be a delay for the new state to actually be active, this is particularly obvious when using group lights.

This leads Alexa to report that the light had an error.

We now cache the state sets by Alexa and return those cached values for up to two seconds.

Fixes #38446

pr_comments: I can't make any sense of the codecov failure; it shows changes in files that haven't been modified and in the file modified change of coverage involve lines that haven't changed (just got shifted due to the comment at the top)

If I understand properly you don't want to break a broken functionality :) 

It's the whole point of this change. HA doesn't currently behave as it should. 

Alexa is reporting a failure only with HA because it is indeed reporting a failure that shouldn't be there in the first place.

You never get to see such failure when using a real Hue hub.
So I don't believe we should ever report a failure, despite this is not a failure per say, it's the read back status that don't match the values set. 

Do we want to fully re-implement the Hue protocol and behave differently, or is the aim to emulate a hue hub?

I believe it should be the latter.

I should add that the failure is reflected in the reachable attribute.

There's also the case where the return we read back will never match the original values.

Due to rounding errors during the 0-255 to 1-254 conversion, we will always return a maximum of 253 I stead of 254.
As it works, the only time we can match is if we set the dimming value to its minimum. Every other cases will mismatch. 

Or the case reported in another bug with a particular dimmer that use different increments.

We will always return a failure which Alexa is very vocal about.

Caching the PUT values makes sense to solve the precision loss of the brightness.  The concern I have is that we are now reporting an assumed success state for 2 seconds after every PUT request.   If alexa didn't care about the success of the request it doesn't seems like they would have implemented a GET right after the PUT as the PUT would have been sufficient if assume success was the intention here.

> 
> 
> Caching the PUT values makes sense to solve the precision loss of the brightness. The concern I have is that we are now reporting an assumed success state for 2 seconds after every PUT request. If alexa didn't care about the success of the request it doesn't seems like they would have implemented a GET right after the PUT as the PUT would have been sufficient if assume success was the intention here.

What Alexa does doesn't always have to make complete sense in regards to what the Hue actually does (wouldn't be a first for Amazon in my personal experience :) )

From the way I've analysed thing, the GET return the state of the controller, not the state of the entity. Otherwise an unreachable light wouldn't see the brightness or the state reported as being correct.

It seems to me that if a failure is to be returned ; it shouldn't be reported in the GET exchange but in the PUT answer.
E.g. we only reply on the PUT after the command has been actually sent to the entities.

But again, we do report a failure in the sense that reachable is the correct value. And Alexa will show a banner if the device is not reachable.

To summarise, what exactly would you like done to approve the fix for this bug?

We can't report the actual value of the brightness nor the colour setting; they won't match.
That leaves only the value of the state to not be cached.

So would you be okay if only the state value wasn't cached?

> 
> So would you be okay if only the state value wasn't cached?

Yes, that is exactly what I am getting at.  If the light fails to turn on, we should report the failure.

> > So would you be okay if only the state value wasn't cached?
> 
> Yes, that is exactly what I am getting at. If the light fails to turn on, we should report the failure.

OK then we need much more logic if we want to do the right thing and remove this 250ms wait.

Not being familiar with the framework, is there an easy way to determine when the action was actually acted upon, so that we only reply to the PUT command once its done.

ok. so bear with me; I've never done any python 3 before today and last I did any real python was a decade ago; so the learning curve isn't minimal.

I have a change that address your concern.
What we will do now is wait for the state change to actually occur before responding to the PUT request.
And for any follow-up GET requests, we will only use the cached values for the attributes other than the state.

issue_context.title: Alexa will often return that a light group is malfunctioning even though it's not
issue_context.body:
## The problem
When you turn on a dimmable light with Alexa via the emulated_hue; the light will turn on, however Alexa will state that the device is malfunctioning.
If the action is performed via the Alexa app, the message "device malfunction" will show at the top or if done via an echo Alexa will say "XXX is malfunctioning"

## Environment
HA 0.113.1

I've tracked the issue in the way the emulated_hue will report the status of the light after it's been turned on or the brightness has been changed.

Here is the typical transaction between Alexa and a real Hue hub (all those were captured via tcpdump):

To turn on:
Alexa -> PUT /api/nouser/lights/4/state {"on":true}
Hue-> [{"success":{"/lights/4/state/on":true}}]
Alexa -> GET /api/nouser/lights/4
Hue-> {"state":{"on":true,"bri":254,"alert":"select","mode":"homeautomation","reachable":true},"swupdate":{"state":"notupdatable","lastinstall":"2020-08-01T00:42:33"},"type":"Dimmable light","name":"Dimmable light 1","modelid":"TRADFRI bulb E27 W opal 1000lm","manufacturername":"IKEA of Sweden","productname":"Dimmable light","capabilities":{"certified":false,"control":{},"streaming":{"renderer":false,"proxy":false}},"config":{"archetype":"classicbulb","function":"functional","direction":"omnidirectional"},"uniqueid":"00:0d:6f:ff:fe:fc:f5:e3-01","swversion":"1.2.214"}
Alexa ->  PUT /api/nouser/lights/4/state {"on":true, "bri": 254}
Hue -> [{"success":{"/lights/19/state/on":true}},{"success":{"/lights/19/state/bri":254}}]
Alexa -> GET /api/nouser/lights/4
Hue -> {"state":{"on":true,"bri":254,"alert":"select","mode":"homeautomation","reachable":true},"swupdate":{"state":"notupdatable","lastinstall":"2020-08-01T00:42:33"},"type":"Dimmable light","name":"Dimmable light 1","modelid":"TRADFRI bulb E27 W opal 1000lm","manufacturername":"IKEA of Sweden","productname":"Dimmable light","capabilities":{"certified":false,"control":{},"streaming":{"renderer":false,"proxy":false}},"config":{"archetype":"classicbulb","function":"functional","direction":"omnidirectional"},"uniqueid":"00:0d:6f:ff:fe:fc:f5:e3-01","swversion":"1.2.214"}

And the transaction is over between the two.

Now when using HA instead this is the typical pattern:
To turn on:
Alexa -> PUT /api/nouser/lights/4/state {"on":true}
HA -> [{"success": {"/lights/4/state/on": true}}]
Alexa -> GET /api/nouser/lights/4
HA -> {"manufacturername": "Home Assistant", "modelid": "HASS123", "name": "Kitchen Bench Lights", "state": {"bri": 1, "mode": "homeautomation", "on": true, "reachable": true}, "swversion": "123", "type": "Dimmable light", "uniqueid": "00:39:2e:2f:49:e5:dd:52-78"}
Alexa -> PUT /api/nouser/lights/4/state {"on":true,"bri":254}
HA -> [{"success": {"/lights/4/state/on": true}}, {"success": {"/lights/4/state/bri": 254}}]
Alexa -> GET /api/nouser/lights/4
HA -> {"manufacturername": "Home Assistant", "modelid": "HASS123", "name": "Kitchen Bench Lights", "state": {"bri": 1, "mode": "homeautomation", "on": true, "reachable": true}, "swversion": "123", "type": "Dimmable light", "uniqueid": "00:39:2e:2f:49:e5:dd:52-78"}
Alexa -> GET /api/nouser/lights/4
HA -> {"manufacturername": "Home Assistant", "modelid": "HASS123", "name": "Kitchen Bench Lights", "state": {"bri": 1, "mode": "homeautomation", "on": true, "reachable": true}, "swversion": "123", "type": "Dimmable light", "uniqueid": "00:39:2e:2f:49:e5:dd:52-78"}
Alexa -> GET /api/nouser/lights/4
HA -> {"manufacturername": "Home Assistant", "modelid": "HASS123", "name": "Kitchen Bench Lights", "state": {"bri": 1, "mode": "homeautomation", "on": true, "reachable": true}, "swversion": "123", "type": "Dimmable light", "uniqueid": "00:39:2e:2f:49:e5:dd:52-78"}
Alexa -> GET /api/nouser/lights/4
HA -> {"manufacturername": "Home Assistant", "modelid": "HASS123", "name": "Kitchen Bench Lights", "state": {"bri": 127, "mode": "homeautomation", "on": true, "reachable": true}, "swversion": "123", "type": "Dimmable light", "uniqueid": "00:39:2e:2f:49:e5:dd:52-78"}
... repeat more
until
HA -> {"manufacturername": "Home Assistant", "modelid": "HASS123", "name": "Kitchen Bench Lights", "state": {"bri": 168, "mode": "homeautomation", "on": true, "reachable": true}, "swversion": "123", "type": "Dimmable light", "uniqueid": "00:39:2e:2f:49:e5:dd:52-78"}

Now we can see that Alexa will set the brightness to 254; and then the HA answer will also be 254. It then immediately query the light for its status.
However, with following gets, the value goes back to being 1; The multiple queries that follows will see the brightness being reported as 1 multiple times, then 127, 165 etc.

For test, I modified the code to only ever return the brightness value to be the same as what Alexa set ; when doing so the device is never reported as malfunctioning.

I've seen this issue happens with a single light bulb though rarely.
When using a light group however, the brightness reported value may take a short while to read back to what it was set.

This is confusing Alexa.

I believe the following GET status request should be the same as what Alexa set, and match the first response data.
comments:
This is the same problem that #35307 attempted to fix. Seems that 250ms isn't enough in some cases.

Typically fixes using random value delays rarely work 100% of the time.

I think a better approach would be to have the following GET always return the value previously set. As Alexa will continue to query over time the value ; following GET can be made to return the actual value.
